## What Problem This Solves

<!--
Describe the concrete user, product, or operational problem.
Use one short, plain-language sentence. For fixes, prefer:
"Fixes: <what goes wrong> when <trigger or condition>."
For other changes, describe the need without inventing a bug.
Name the affected workflow, not the code-level cause.

Fixes: Companion becomes Not Responding when chat scrolls to the newest message past a tall, virtualized history row.

## User Impact

<!--
"User impact: <what users, operators, or developers can now do or expect>."
Lead with the concrete outcome in plain language, usually one sentence.
For internal-only changes, say there is no user-visible change; do not invent a benefit.
Keep important risks, breaking changes, migrations, and required user actions visible here.
-->

User impact: opening history, following new messages, and remounting chat remain responsive without taking readers back to the bottom after they scroll up. This is a source fix, not an update to an already-running installed Companion.

Full-application acceptance is still incomplete: the follow-up below found a clipped streamed tail after returning from Notifications, and reader scroll-up retention is not yet demonstrated in the full app. This is not a ready-to-merge claim.

The three previously failing 1007-pixel native cases are repaired in `bc2f2774`: the 19-case selection passed, and all five history-tail cases passed ten fresh processes (50/50), followed by a committed-head rebuild/run (5/5). Full-application, foreground-input and Release acceptance remain incomplete.

These are regression cases introduced by this PR in `b98c89bc`, not existing default-branch CI tests. Baseline comparisons transplanted the tests onto unchanged default production; they must not be described as default-branch CI failures.

## Why This Change Was Made

<!--
Briefly explain how the change addresses the problem without repeating the impact.
Keep the body short. Leave file lists, internal acronyms, and root-cause walkthroughs
in the diff or optional <details>; include technical detail only when it explains
behavior or a material tradeoff. Do not hide risks or required actions in <details>.
-->

The live stack and synthetic native reproduction both blocked inside `ItemsView.StartBringItemIntoView`. This fix avoids its synchronous realization/layout boundary, rather than assuming recursive `LayoutUpdated` re-entry. Reactor still owns the stable-key list and virtualization.

Native geometry drives the asynchronous scroll. Recycling before an offset is issued retries normal layout; recycling after issuance preserves the valid native correlation instead of endlessly replacing the request. If the settled target was lost, a generation-fenced retry resolves live coordinates after anchor retention.

Owned native completions, including canceled brings and replaced offsets, are distinguished from reader navigation. Reader completion cancels pending retries and supersedes a still-issued tail offset at the observed reader position. Each new explicit history request establishes a native boundary so an older reader completion cannot cancel the newer jump. Correlation ordering and wrap handling follow the SDK's [31-bit counter implementation](https://github.com/microsoft/microsoft-ui-xaml/blob/d8915cf00984489da2541fc2328818ec23baa466/controls/dev/ScrollPresenter/ScrollPresenter.cpp#L3331), with focused boundary/wrap coverage.

## Summary

```diff
 tail request
-  ItemsView.StartBringItemIntoView (synchronous layout)
+  realize through normal native layout
+  request native target geometry asynchronously
+  preserve issued offsets when their containers recycle
+  retarget lost settled anchors using live coordinates
+  honor current reader navigation; fence stale completions
```

## Evidence

<!--
Show the most useful proof that this change works. Screenshots, screencasts,
terminal output, focused tests, CI results, live observations, redacted logs,
and artifact links are all useful. Include before/after evidence for visual
changes when it clarifies the result.

validation easy to understand, not to restate the diff.
Summarize what was checked and the result; note meaningful gaps. Link long output
or put it in optional <details>, keeping the useful evidence summary visible.
-->

- **Before:** a synthetic production-root history with 16 mixed-role messages, one tall assistant row away from the end, and an unrealized newest row reproduced the UI-thread spin in `StartBringItemIntoView`. A task-owned external watchdog was needed to stop the frozen test host. The live Gateway health/readiness endpoints were responsive. [Sanitized investigation](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw-windows-node/issues/1568#issuecomment-6513417778).
- **Current repair (2026-11-04, `bc2f2774`):** full build, 55 focused contracts, 4,809 Shared tests and 4,796 Tray tests passed. Native siblings: **19/19**; complete chat-layout class: **130 passed, 2 existing gated skips**; ten fresh five-case runs: **50/50**; committed-head rebuilt regression: **5/5**. Native viewport assertions and deadlines were retained; reader navigation is now exercised immediately after the tail appears, plus an older scroll before a newer explicit jump.
- **Historical conflict-resolution check (2026-11-03):** merged upstream `b917d7e1` in `a151396d`. Native selection was **16 passed, 3 failed**; the exact pre-merge-controller comparison reproduced those case identities. That comparison was not pristine default production.
- **Original-head after (historical, `b98c89bc`):** all five native regression cases passed at 320/800/1007 pixels, including append and remount. The wide case also verified scroll-up retention when a message arrived and an explicit subsequent history jump. A 19-case native sibling selection passed; a fresh-process five-case repetition and a further committed-head rebuild/run also passed, with no selected skips.
- **Current independent review:** bounded Copilot `code-review` follow-ups identified two P2 cancellation/generation gaps; both were fixed and disposed of at source level, with no remaining high-confidence finding in that scope. Model identity is unverified. This is not a canonical-helper result, native scheduling certification, or complete proof-pool acceptance.
- **Historical original-head review:** GPT-6 Astra reviewed the Standards and Spec axes with no significant issues reported. The canonical isolated autoreview helper additionally completed its P0-P3 implementation/proof-plan review with Codex/GPT-6 Luna: three complete passes, `scoped-clean`, no findings. Its default Sol models were unavailable for the account; Luna was selected from that account's model catalog without changing isolation or authentication settings.

The original installed native WinUI 3.2 binary was not retested. Native proof here uses the repository's current SDK/runtime, not a claim that the complete maintainer proof pool ran.

## Validation

### Current repair: 2026-11-04

Commit: `bc2f27744463fbea9b8a77ac7173e107cb01e53c`. Pre-commit checks used recorded tree `cbda8dd433e1c13efde5dcb953379b29c37eb9e7`; the committed tree was verified identical, then the native project was rebuilt and all five regressions executed again on the committed head. The four paths are the positioner, existing `TailNavigationPolicy`, source/policy tests and native regression file.

Before editing, fetched default `main` at `12789b405719c5755955674f37fa09ad0eb07b3d` and inspected its 15 commits after `b917d7e1`: no equivalent native-tail fix had landed. The affected controller, policy and regression source were unchanged between those default tips; reconnect PR #1795 does not repair this scroll path.

| --- | --- |
| `.\build.ps1` | Passed |
| `dotnet test .\tests\OpenClaw.Shared.Tests\OpenClaw.Shared.Tests.csproj --no-restore` | 4,809 passed, 0 failed, 25 existing skipped |
| `dotnet test .\tests\OpenClaw.Tray.Tests\OpenClaw.Tray.Tests.csproj --no-restore` | 4,796 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped |

| Native test project with `--no-build --no-restore -c Debug -r win-x64 --filter "FullyQualifiedName~ReactorChatLayoutProofTests"` | 130 passed, 0 failed, 2 existing gated skips |
| Same native project with `--filter "FullyQualifiedName~HistoryTail_"`, ten fresh processes | 50 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped |

| Rebuilt committed-head `HistoryTail_` selector | 5 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped |
| Changed controller/policy/unit-test whitespace verification and `git diff --cached --check` | Passed |

The two whole-class skips require the explicitly authorized native keyboard and parent-owned pointer/capture drivers. Neither was enabled or claimed as proof. Exact native labels, filters, counts and source/binary hashes were retained; no selected history-tail or 19-case proof was skipped. The new boundary policy's eight cases first exposed three rejection failures under unconditional admission, then passed with the request-boundary comparison.

**Attribution, not CI history:** a separate 22-execution comparison used pristine `b917d7e1` production plus this PR's transplanted regression tests. Append failed 3/3 on both default production and `a151`; append/remount failed 1/3 on default and 3/3 on `a151`. The wide reader/jump case failed 3/3 on each, but at different stages (default: reader scroll-up; PR: later explicit jump). Therefore the failures were not all proven newly introduced, and the exact jump failure was not proven pre-existing. All were directly coupled acceptance gaps, rather than tests to remove.

**Not verified / blocked:** current-head complete-Companion acceptance, original installed runtime, real provider/Gateway replay and the complete interactive proof pool. The last Debug full-app attempt on an earlier candidate passed **0/2** (UIA deadline and natural message-240 tail); it was not a current-head pass or proven environment-only failure. Release proof is blocked by the required signed cleanup executable (`OpenClawSignedCleanupHostPath`), without changing signing/trust settings. Correctly isolated gallery controls separately failed to obtain foreground (`HWND=0`); no manual admission was fabricated.

Earlier exploratory whole-native attempts are not accepted suite results: one aborted in a COM finalizer after 509 passes/155 failures (154 missing-isolation-root prerequisites and one residual tail geometry failure), and one malformed external selector hit its watchdog. The final typed runner checked exact label/filter identity and case counts. An earlier intermediate 19-case run also hit the question-composer visibility assertion; default production passed that isolated case six times and the final candidate passed it in all three 19-case runs, which does not establish causality for the earlier failure.

### Conflict resolution: 2026-11-03 (historical)

Merge commit: `a151396deb7471cfa1a64a0058dd5bcd83b0149a`, integrating upstream `b917d7e197e5194a14577a290805be4d13c409be`. Tests ran before commit on recorded tree `37f34f282812334f5ac741f4d5441f12d9e1eb0e`; the committed tree was verified identical.

At this historical merge, the resolution kept upstream `InitialTailNavigationRequest.TryResolve` inside the dispatcher, with its originating generation, and retained low-priority asynchronous native navigation. `renderAfterLayout` propagated into target-recycling retries, preserving reflow follow/input guards. One upstream source assertion was adapted to this combined call contract. That revision's delta was confined to the original three paths.

| Historical merged-tree check | Actual result |
| --- | --- |
| `.\build.ps1 -NoTrustRepository` | All 5 production projects passed; 69 Markdown files validated |
| `dotnet test .\tests\OpenClaw.Tray.Tests\OpenClaw.Tray.Tests.csproj --no-restore --filter "FullyQualifiedName~ChatTimelinePresentationTests"` | 47 passed, 0 failed |

| Same-environment comparison using the byte-identical pre-merge `ac55e1e6` controller, `HistoryTail_` selector | **2 passed, 3 failed**; the same three failing case identities |
| `git diff --cached --check`, unresolved-index check, tested-tree/commit equality | Passed |

The native command is the 19-case selector shown in the historical command block below, run under a task-owned 90-second external watchdog. Its failures are the 1007-pixel append, append/remount, and explicit-history-jump cases. The UI dispatcher remains runnable, but the newest marker does not reach the viewport. These tests were not skipped, weakened or reported as passing. The comparison changes only the controller back to its exact pre-merge content; it is not a clean full-binary execution of the old commit.

The first native attempt had 13 failures because its existing restore graph still selected Reactor preview.12 while the product used preview.16. Running `dotnet restore .\tests\OpenClaw.Tray.UITests\OpenClaw.Tray.UITests.csproj -r win-x64 --configfile <task-local-config>` aligned both graphs to upstream preview.16. The restored run and final rebuilt candidate both retained the three behavioral failures above. Restores used the previously documented trusted HTTPS proxy, without disabling audit, TLS, trust or test safeguards.

A bounded independent Copilot `code-review` implementation/proof-plan review found no significant integration issues at that revision. This was source review, not runtime acceptance. At that time the three native failures remained open; the current repair above supersedes that result, not the full-app, hosted-CI or Notifications-return/physical-reader proof gaps.

### 2026-11-02 conflict-resolution update (historical)

The branch integrates `main` at `a4dd026cc5f85a444a0fcd05eef5b86282dbda8c`. The resolution preserves asynchronous native tail navigation alongside upstream resize/reflow correction and user-input cancellation, including cancellation cleanup and the reflow gates when a recycled target is rebound.

Resolution commit: `ac55e1e61a89dac0ddb4ba15150570043ae2817f`.

The passing totals above and the runtime evidence below belong to the earlier head `b98c89bcee5249177c4dc564064f4828a0ae7425`. They are not current-head test results. The resolved source tree is `b48cb69d4adf2dd04dcff08317185e3d66b98368`.

Independent Copilot P0-P3 review identified the reflow-gate propagation issue, and the same reviewer's final bounded follow-up confirmed it closed with no unresolved findings on this exact tree. ## Real Behavior Proof

### Current native source: 2026-11-04

Tested source tree: `cbda8dd433e1c13efde5dcb953379b29c37eb9e7`, committed unchanged as `bc2f27744463fbea9b8a77ac7173e107cb01e53c`, then rebuilt for the committed-head run. Environment: Windows x64, aligned Reactor preview.16, current repository WinUI SDK/runtime, isolated synthetic production Reactor root. This is native-root execution, not a complete Companion observation or original installed-runtime replay.

```text
Entire ReactorChatLayoutProofTests class: 130 passed; 0 failed; 2 gated skips
HistoryTail_ (ten fresh processes):       50 passed; 0 failed; 0 skipped
Final native lifecycle/root selection:   19 passed; 0 failed; 0 skipped
Committed-head rebuilt HistoryTail_:      5 passed; 0 failed; 0 skipped
```

The wide case now scrolls away immediately when the newest marker becomes visible, verifies top-position retention across ordinary append, then verifies a new explicit history jump despite an older native scroll. Before the repair, traces showed a still-issued tail offset applying after the reader reached zero; ignoring its late callback alone did not stop that native movement.

No current-head public screenshot/video link or completed interactive/full-app pool is claimed. The historical negative observations below remain open until rechecked on a qualified host.

### Merged source: 2026-11-03 (historical)

The current merge commit `a151396deb7471cfa1a64a0058dd5bcd83b0149a` has the exact tested source tree `37f34f282812334f5ac741f4d5441f12d9e1eb0e`. Native execution used aligned Reactor preview.16 and an isolated synthetic production-root test host, not a new full-application observation. The pre-commit binary's informational version names the first parent `ac55e1e6`; source correspondence is established by the recorded tree, not by claiming a post-commit binary run.

```text
HistoryTail_ at width 320: passed
HistoryTail_ at width 800: passed
HistoryTail_ at width 1007: append, append/remount, explicit jump failed
```

At this historical revision the three native cases were failing. The current repair supersedes those native results; full-app behavior, original installed runtime, real provider/Gateway replay and the complete proof pool remain unverified. Earlier visible full-app observations below are retained as historical evidence only.

### Original native-root proof (`b98c89bc`, historical)

- Environment tested: Windows x64, .NET SDK 10.0.403/runtime 10.0.14, current Windows App SDK 2.6.4/native WinUI 3.3, isolated production Reactor root with a synthetic provider.

- Screenshot or artifact links verified? (`Yes`/`No`/`N/A`) N/A. No public image/artifact attachment is claimed; copied execution output is above.

### Full-application follow-up (2026-10-30, historical partial)

This follow-up used a separate **production `OpenClaw.Tray.WinUI.exe` process**, not the in-process Reactor test host. The existing `OpenClaw.GatewayFixtureHost` launched it with `--scenario chat-interactive --duration-seconds 1200` and a disposable profile. The production Gateway client, history loader, provider, shell and timeline were exercised; the loopback Gateway and conversation data were synthetic. No real model/provider or host command executed.

The app's informational version contains head `b98c89bcee5249177c4dc564064f4828a0ae7425`; its product DLL SHA-256 is `A266D8927C5E09F75CEDBFE193EEB729AA438F0EB80317DE360138B33FFF8DBA`. The loaded native XAML version was `3.3.0.0`. No source changes were made for this follow-up.

Steps: select **Fixture: 240-message conversation** without scrolling it first; inspect its last row; send one synthetic message through the discovered `app.chat.send`; wait for the fixture stream to finish; switch to the main conversation and back; then open **Notifications > Open notifications > Back**.

Copied native UI diagnostics from the initial selection and completed append:

```text
Window: "OpenClaw" 1280x860
OwnerDetail: Connected

Initial history selection:
AXTable Chat messages screen@785,570 1007x646
AXStaticText FIXTURE LONG END 240 screen@921,1139 736x21

After synthetic streaming append:
AXTable Chat messages screen@785,570 1007x646
AXStaticText FIXTURE INTERACTIVE COMPLETE screen@921,1139 736x21
```

In both observations the final marker's complete vertical bounds, 1139..1160, were inside the actual transcript viewport, 570..1216. `app.chat.snapshot` subsequently reported `selectedTimeline.turnActive=false` and retained the complete final answer ending in `FIXTURE INTERACTIVE COMPLETE`. Switching away to the main session and reselecting the long session also restored this fully visible tail. These are manual full-process observations, not additional automated test passes.

**Remaining negative result:** after Notifications > Back, the app still responded and the snapshot still contained the complete answer, but the native visible subtree ended partway through its table and did not expose the final marker. Reselecting the long session restored it. This recurred after a controlled reselection with no intervening scroll attempt, so route-return/remount tail visibility is **not accepted**. Whether this clipping predates the patch has not been established.

**Other limits:** background scroll/key attempts did not establish a verifiable reader scroll-up position, so full-app reader-position retention remains unproven. The 240-message full-app fixture is not the minimized 16-message giant-row case; that exact trigger still has native-root test-host evidence only. The existing full-app UIA attempt timed out at its 150-second worker deadline and was not a passing proof run. No public media attachment, original installed-runtime replay, real-provider replay, complete proof-pool result or cleared merge gate is claimed.

title: fix(chat): chat freezes when opening tall message history
